what_it_does: Family metals group founded in 1962 (HQ 1700 W Fulton St, Chicago). It recovers copper and aluminum from insulated, armored and oilfield cable, processes and trades metal, and is growing PVC cable-jacket recycling.
link_to_trend:
Strongest link in the portfolio.
• Two sources of scrap: retired transformers, and the production scrap that builders generate. Both carry copper and aluminum windings, steel tanks and cores, and oil.
• Steady feedstock: the installed base is 60-80M units, with about 1.5-2.7M replaced a year (computed).
• Copper prices help: copper is about $14,474/t (+45% YoY), and Section 232 duties on refined copper (15% in 2027, 30% in 2028) raise the value of domestic secondary copper.
• Addressable market (est.): $30-120M/yr for retired-unit buyback (f2) and $20-80M/yr for closed-loop copper chops to rod mills (f1). These are estimates, not sales, and they overlap.
action:
Run a teardown pilot in the next 6 months.
• Sign 3-5 supply agreements for retired units with Midwest utilities, co-ops and municipal utilities.
• Sign 2-3 production-scrap buyback agreements with transformer plants within trucking range: Prolec GE and Eaton in Waukesha WI, and WEG in Washington MO.
• Confirm oil-handling and PCB permits and indemnities before taking any units. PCB rules come from general knowledge, not the research.
• Decide by mid-2027 whether to buy a regional transformer dismantler (Play 1).

what_it_does: Wire and cable processor in Jonesboro IN that granulates insulated copper and aluminum wire into clean metal chops.
link_to_trend: Utility reconductoring, undergrounding and cable replacement raise volumes of utility cable scrap. Clean #1 copper chops are the only form a rod mill can feed into the winding-wire chain. Whether Southwire uses scrap feed is unconfirmed.
action: Submit #1 chops for qualification at one rod mill. Southwire and Freeport's rod mills are in the value-chain map, but neither is confirmed to accept scrap. Process magnet-wire and cable scrap from the teardown pilot. Add granulation capacity only after the pilot shows volume.

what_it_does: Non-ferrous scrap buyer and processor in Northlake IL: insulated wire, copper, aluminum and brass.
link_to_trend: A natural Chicago-area collection point for scrap from utilities, electrical contractors, transformer rebuilders and data-center construction offcuts. That includes winding copper and bushing brass.
action: Open accounts with Chicago-area electrical contractors and data-center construction sites. Serve as the drop-off yard for the teardown pilot. Track volume and margin by source every month so the pilot can be judged by mid-2027.

what_it_does: Chicago producer of zinc alloys and zinc anodes for galvanizing, plating, cathodic protection and die casting.
link_to_trend:
Indirect.
• Galvanizing: zinc goes into hot-dip galvanizing of transmission towers, substation steel and some pad-mount hardware.
• Anodes: zinc anodes protect buried substation steel.
• Timing: demand rises mostly in 2028-34 as transmission projects are built, including ERCOT's 765 kV plan (about 2,468 mi) and MISO Tranche 2.1 (3,631 mi).
• No direct sales to transformer makers.
action: List the current galvanizer customers that serve utility-structure and substation-steel fabricators. Use the list to screen galvanizers as possible acquisitions (Play 7). No capex.

what_it_does: Secondary aluminum smelter in Minerva OH that turns scrap into die-cast and foundry alloys.
link_to_trend:
Weak to moderate. It cannot make the EC-grade (1350) aluminum used for windings. It can do two things:
• Absorb clean aluminum winding scrap from teardowns.
• Sell alloy to foundries that cast bushing flanges, terminal pads and enclosure parts. Addressable market is est. $10-45M/yr (f3), not current sales.
action: Send aluminum windings from the teardown pilot to Minerva and test what they are worth as a high-purity addition to the melt. Line up alloy supply for any foundry FAM buys under Play 3.

what_it_does: Calls itself the largest US maker of non-battery lead products: sheet, brick, radiation shielding, ballast and shot. Runs a rolling mill in Birmingham AL and a shot tower in Granite City IL.
link_to_trend: Limited. Lead has no direct use in transformers. The only niches are lead-alloy sheathing for high-voltage underground and submarine cable, and radiation shielding.
action: No grid program. Answer inquiries for cable-sheathing alloy as they come in; do not invest.

what_it_does: Milwaukee foundry making stainless and high-alloy sand and investment castings up to about 200 lb for energy, nuclear and power-generation OEMs. Lead times are about 6 weeks.
link_to_trend:
Moderate.
• What it can make: stainless valve bodies, cooler flanges, and tap-changer (OLTC) and bushing hardware.
• Tap changers: Reinhausen expanded its Humboldt TN plant 45% and plans to double global capacity by 2030; many of its castings still come from Germany. Addressable est. $1-5M/yr (f6).
• Bushings: Trench's Charlotte bushing plant opened in Jul 2026.
• Hitachi: addressable est. $2-10M/yr (f7).
• Adjacent market: turbine and generator OEMs (GE Vernova backlog 116 GW, Siemens Energy 69 GW) supplying data-center power.
action: In Q4 2026, send capability packages and request RFQs from Reinhausen (Humboldt TN), Trench (Charlotte NC), Hubbell PCORE (LeRoy NY), Hitachi Energy and Qualitrol. Lead with the 6-week lead time. Target one approved first-article order by mid-2027.

what_it_does: Maker of cast steel shot and grit from melted scrap in Canton Township MI. One of three leading US producers; claims to be the only North American maker of a low-carbon shot.
link_to_trend:
A direct consumable, but the pool is small.
• Use: tanks, radiators, pad-mount cabinets, switchgear and substation steel are blasted before painting.
• Pool size (est.): $2-8M/yr chain-wide; outsourced shops $0.3-2.8M (f4) and Howard $0.3-2M (f5).
• Effect on Metaltec: even large share gains are a few percent of its estimated $20-50M revenue.
action:
Win the abrasive specification on blast lines that start up in 2026-27:
• PTT Raeford pad-mount plant
• Eaton Jonesville
• ERMCO Waddell
• JST Wytheville
• Howard Ellisville
• Prolec Goldsboro
• VTC Rincon
• HD Hyundai Montgomery #2
• Hyosung Memphis

Lead with the low-carbon shot. Use existing distributors where they already cover a plant.

what_it_does: Swiss-type CNC turning and Metalflow zinc cast-in-place assemblies in Walled Lake MI. About 40 staff and about $5.4M revenue (weak source).
link_to_trend: Weak to moderate. Panther could make turned terminals, studs and bushing hardware for distribution transformers and meters. The pool is est. $8-38M/yr, of which Eaton's share is est. $1-6M (f10). No grid customers were found.
action: Quote 2-3 turned-hardware part families to Eaton (Waukesha WI) and one other distribution builder. Drop the effort if no part is approved (PPAP) within 9 months. This does not justify capex.

what_it_does: Aluminum, composite and vinyl building products, plus CNC fabrication and contract manufacturing, at plants in Alexandria LA, Olive Branch MS, Pell City AL and Olmstead IL. About 300-400 staff; est. $60-110M revenue. FAM acquired it in Jul 2025.
link_to_trend:
Moderate, with the best location in the portfolio.
• Location: the plants sit near Howard (MS), Prolec Shreveport (LA), Hitachi Crystal Springs/Gallman (MS), HD Hyundai Montgomery (AL) and Central Moloney Pine Bluff (AR).
• Can make: parts that do not need to hold pressure, such as cabinet doors, sills, platforms, guards and brackets, plus aluminum or stainless enclosures for coastal utilities.
• Cannot make: sealed transformer tanks; it is not a tank-welding shop.
• Addressable market (est.): $3-20M at Howard (f8) and $3-25M at Eaton (f9). Both are subsets of builders' outsourced tank and enclosure spend.
action: Pick the plant with spare fabrication capacity. Quote enclosure sub-assemblies to Howard, Prolec Shreveport and HD Hyundai Montgomery by Q1 2027. Win a paid first-article order before any capex. Screen tank fabricators as an add-on only if a builder commits volume (Play 5).

what_it_does: Chicago aviation aftermarket platform: aircraft and engine leasing, teardown, parts inventory and repair. Bought a majority of J&C Aero (Vilnius) in 2026.
link_to_trend: None. The only tie is aircraft-teardown aluminum and titanium scrap that could go to Imperial.
action: No grid action. Keep sending teardown scrap to Imperial when the pricing works.

what_it_does: Chicago 3PL and freight broker: flatbed, dry van, drayage, cross-dock and warehousing, with Mexico-US-Canada lanes. About $43M revenue (weak source).
link_to_trend:
Moderate for distribution-size freight.
• Mexico flows: Mexico supplied 45% of US core imports in 2019. It is also a source of magnet wire (Magnekon) and finished units (Prolec Monterrey, Eaglerise and Jinpan Mexico).
• Addressable market (est.): $10-40M for Prolec freight (f11) and $12-45M for imported distribution units (f12).
• No heavy haul: Transend cannot move large power units.
action:
Within 6 months:
• Quote Monterrey-to-US flatbed lanes to Prolec GE, Worthington's Corefficient (cores) and Magnekon.
• Set up reverse logistics from utility yards to Imperial for the teardown pilot.
• Do not buy heavy-haul equipment.

what_it_does: AS9100-certified CNC machining for aerospace, defense and firearms in the Atlanta area. FAM partnered with it around mid-2026; the founders still run it.
link_to_trend: Weak. Machined parts for switchgear, tap changers or test equipment are possible, but no grid customers were found. FAM is not in control.
action: No grid program. Keep the focus on aerospace and defense.
